content:
**Spanish men who have won the French Open (Roland Garros) since 1990 and the date they first reached their career‑high ATP singles ranking**

| Player | French Open titles (since 1990) | Career‑high ranking achieved | Date first reached that ranking* |
|--------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Sergi Bruguera** | 1993, 1994 | World No. 4 (his highest ATP ranking) | **07/05/1994** |
| **Juan Carlos Ferrero** | 2003 | World No. 1 | **09/08/2003** |
| **Rafael Nadal** | 2005‑2022 (14 titles) | World No. 1 | **08/18/2008** |

\* ATP rankings are published weekly (usually on Monday). The dates shown are the **first Monday** on which each player appeared at his career‑high position.

### Quick notes
- **Sergi Bruguera** became the first Spanish man in the modern era to win Roland Garros (1993) and defended the title in 1994. His peak ranking of No. 4 was first recorded in the ATP list released **5 July 1994**.  
- **Juan Carlos Ferrero** lifted the French Open trophy in **June 2003** and, after a strong second half of the season, ascended to the top of the rankings for the first time on **8 September 2003**.  
- **Rafael Nadal** captured his inaugural Roland Garros crown in **June 2005** and, after winning Wimbledon 2008, broke the No. 1 barrier on **18 August 2008** – a ranking he has held (in total) for a record‑breaking number of weeks.  

These three Spaniards are the only male players from Spain to have won the French Open singles title from 1990 onward, and the dates above mark when each first reached the highest ATP ranking of his career.
